questions.subject: SPANISH
questions.topic: The plural of a word ending in z
questions.learningObjective: Explain how a noun ending in z forms its plural
questions.stem: A planner asks how the plural of 'lápiz' is formed on the route sign; explain the rule.

answer.exemplar: The plural of a word ending in z replaces the z with c and then adds es, so lápiz becomes lápices, and the same pattern gives peces from pez.

questions.explanation: The final z becomes c before adding es, producing lápices. Simply adding s or es to z is not accepted in standard spelling.
questions.hint: Replace z with c, then add es.

questions.subject: SPANISH
questions.topic: The stress of a singular and of its plural, and the two documented exceptions
questions.stem: Explain the plural of 'crimen' on the board.

answer.exemplar: Crimen follows the documented exception: its plural is crímenes, shifting the stress to the penultimate syllable and taking a written accent.

questions.explanation: Crimen becomes crímenes with stress on the penultimate syllable and a written accent.
questions.hint: The plural shifts stress and takes an accent.

questions.subject: SPANISH
questions.topic: The plural of a word ending in z

stimulus.body: A board lists the plural forms of nouns ending in z. The planner must explain why the letter changes before the suffix is added.

questions.stem: Which plural of 'luz' is correct?

options.misconception: adds s without changing z to c

options.text: luzez, keeping z and adding ez
options.misconception: keeps z instead of changing it to c

options.text: luces, replacing z with c and adding es

questions.explanation: Luz becomes luces. The z becomes c and then es is added.
questions.hint: z becomes c, then add es.

questions.topic: The feminine nouns of everyday life
questions.stem: Explain why the board writes 'la foto' for the photo notice.

answer.exemplar: Foto is feminine in everyday Spanish despite ending in o, so the board writes la foto rather than el foto.
